admission.justification: The Jump-only behavior and the answered-only reveal were weighed and rejected, and every later change to how a tree row or a kept family is selected has to decide what the stacked layout shows and what it leaves to the reader's next action.

alternatives.option: An in-tree subject selection on the stacked layout reveals the start of its reading area: the answer when it arrives, and the failed or refused status once the read ends unavailable. Focus stays on the selected row, and a status reveal moves no focus and leaves the focus request for a retry.
alternatives.reason: OR-R033 required the reading area to be visible without an additional Jump, and OR-R042 ruled that the requirement reaches a failed or refused read as well as an answered one; the reveal follows the existing focus guard and the existing 60rem breakpoint.

alternatives.option: Keep the explicit Jump control as the only way to the reading area, as before the ruling.
alternatives.reason: An in-tree selection that appears to do nothing until the reader finds a second control is the measured defect the ruling exists to fix.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The stacked layout stops placing the reading area below a tall tree, so a selection already shows its answer without a reveal.

alternatives.option: Reveal only when the read is answered; a failed or refused selection keeps the view where it was.
alternatives.reason: OR-R042 closed this alternative: the failed or refused status is what the reading area has to show for that selection, and the owner ruled there is no answered-only exception.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The status of a failed or refused read is shown somewhere the reader already sees, so the reading area need not be revealed for it.

consequences: On the stacked layout an in-tree selection scrolls the reading-area column to its start and focuses the selected row with `preventScroll`, so one activation reads, reveals and keeps the tree.
A failed or refused read reveals its own status without moving focus and without using up the selection's focus request, so a successful retry still follows the answer path.

A reader who moved focus while the read was on its way keeps both focus and the viewport; a lane destination and an opened file, which OR-R033 leaves unchanged, still do not reveal at the stacked layout.
context: On the stacked layout (60rem and narrower) the family tree stands above the reading area, and the reading area can begin thousands of pixels below the viewport. A selection of a row the tree shows read its subject, kept the tree and moved focus onto the row, but the answer (and, for a failed or refused read, the status that stands for it) stayed out of view until the reader found the explicit Jump control. This leaf's Worker's narrow probe of 2026-10-06 measured the answer 11,849 pixels below an 844-pixel viewport. OR-R033 asked for an ordinary-meaning correction; OR-R042 closed the answered-only reading of that ruling.
